summary: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller input until it reaches a base case it can answer directly. Use it when a problem breaks into a smaller copy of itself.
notes: Every recursive function needs a base case, like if n <= 1: return 1, that makes no further call.
n // 10 drops the last digit, so each call to sum_of_digits works on a shorter number.
sys.getrecursionlimit() is 1000 by default, so depth(5000) raises RecursionError.
pitfall: A missing or unreachable base case, like if n == 1 when n starts at 0, makes the calls never stop and ends in RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded.
